topic: Troubleshooting from logs: journalctl, systemctl, configuration
title: The department website is down
instructions:
## Nobody can open the department website

The night technician "fixed something" and left. Apache is installed on this server, but the site is down. You are **root**.

## Do this

Work from the evidence, not from guesses:

1. `systemctl status apache2` and `journalctl -u apache2` tell you why it will not start. Fix the configuration file named in the error.
2. Start the service and **enable** it so it survives a reboot.
3. `curl http://localhost/` should return the page. If it does not, check that the document root `/srv/www/htdocs/index.html` exists (the backup is in `/var/backups`).
4. The firewall must allow **http**: `firewall-cmd --list-services`, then add the service permanently and reload.
5. Press **Check my work**.

logs: AH00526: Syntax error on line 1 of /etc/apache2/listen.conf:
apache2.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
Failed to start The Apache Webserver.

faults.message: AH00526: Syntax error on line 1 of /etc/apache2/listen.conf: Port must be specified
AH00112: Warning: DocumentRoot [/srv/www/htdocs] does not exist

files./etc/apache2/listen.conf:
# Port the server listens on
Listen 8o
files./var/log/apache2/error_log: [Tue Oct 21 23:41:02 2026] [core:error] AH00526: Syntax error on line 1 of /etc/apache2/listen.conf: Port must be specified

hints: journalctl -u apache2 shows "Port must be specified" on line 1 of listen.conf: the letter o was typed instead of the digit 0.
After fixing the file, apachectl configtest should say Syntax OK. Then systemctl enable --now apache2.
The document root was deleted. Restore it from the archive: tar -xzf /var/backups/htdocs-2026-10-20.tar.gz -C /

checks.label: You read the logs first
checks.message: Use journalctl -u apache2 or systemctl status apache2 to see why it failed.

realityNote: The order you used is the troubleshooting method from the course: symptom, service status, logs, configuration test, fix, verify locally, then check the network path (firewall). Writing the steps into a runbook is what turns one fix into a repeatable one.
